reuse.why: Replaces four copied midpoint computations with a new shared getExpectedAmount (on top of the existing getApproxNumberThreshold) and routes getScheduledAmount and the API through it, but the preview and budget-template sites only partly use it.

duplication.why: computeSchedulePreviewTransactions keeps its own missing/number/range dispatch (calling only getRangedAmount, so approx is skipped) and schedule-template keeps its own op dispatch around getExpectedAmount, both re-deciding what the helper already decides.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, and the server, forecast, template and API layers import it.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field; release notes are per-step, and getScheduledAmount gains an op argument that the desktop callers never pass.

maintainability.why: Two overlapping public entry points (getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount with inverse/op) plus two call sites with their own dispatch make it easy for approximate amounts to be handled inconsistently across views.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions uses getRangedAmount inside its own null/number/range dispatch instead of getExpectedAmount; server/budget/schedule-template.ts keeps its own isbetween/isapprox dispatch.

disguised_duplication.where: The leftover dispatches in computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and createScheduleList are the old open structure with the inner arm swapped, not reshaped copies.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter that parallels the new getExpectedAmount; computeSchedulePreviewTransactions (shared/schedules.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) keep their own dispatch around the helpers.
